subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both options change where provider OAuth material may be acquired, persisted, or transferred across the node/gateway boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent credential-boundary behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback and tunnel setups.

options.title: Design credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-owned flow that moves provider auth material to the gateway store without first consuming or persisting it on the node.

options.title: Warn but permit
options.body: Keep local-write behavior with a strong warning, accepting the wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback and tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the maintainer draft for this exact fix direction and is a recent contributor on the auth CLI surface.
